settings.description: Leave your boots by the stove. There’s a map on the table and a whole ridge outside the door.

settings.title: Under one roof
settings.subtitle: THE HUT
settings.description: Four bunkrooms share a long kitchen table, a boot porch and a drying room. On wet afternoons the warden clears the supper maps away for cards.

settings.title: From the doorstep
settings.subtitle: DAY WALKS
settings.description: Pick up a paper map at breakfast. The warden marks closures and muddy stretches on the porch board each morning.

items.title: Spruce Loop
items.description: Follow the little green tree markers from the woodshed. At the split spruce, take the lower fork back to the kitchen garden.

items.title: Mill Beck
items.description: Take the mill path as far as the stone bridge. The wide bank just before the bridge makes a good place for a packed lunch.

items.title: West Saddle
items.description: Ask the warden about visibility before leaving. Beyond the last trees the path is exposed. Return by the same marked route.

settings.title: The kitchen clock
settings.subtitle: HUT HOURS
settings.description: Supper is served at one sitting. Tell the kitchen at breakfast if you’ll be back late.

static_rows.cells: 07:00–08:30|Porridge, toast and hot tea in the kitchen

tabs.tab_content: Come through the porch and sign the guest book at the warden’s desk. If you expect to arrive after the desk closes, agree on an arrival plan with your host before setting off.

tabs.tab_title: What should I bring for the bunkroom?
tabs.tab_content: Pack a sleeping liner, towel and headlamp. Bring clean indoor shoes and keep muddy boots on the porch rack.
Add your name to the kitchen list before supper. Collect your lunch during breakfast and bring your own refillable bottle.
